title: The average of cos squared over a cycle
spoken: The average over a cycle of cosine squared of omega t equals one half.
explanation: cos² rises and falls between 0 and 1, and over a whole cycle it spends as long above one half as below it, so its average is exactly one half. A detector that responds to the square of the field records half the peak.
assumptions: The average is taken over a whole number of cycles.
A foundation lesson's worked case in modern notation; not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Averaged over whole cycles, cos squared is exactly one half.

notes.title: Averaged over a cycle
notes.explanation: The mean value over whole cycles, which is what a slow detector sees.

notes.title: Squared
notes.explanation: The energy a wave delivers goes as the square of its field.

notes.title: Cosine
notes.explanation: Rises and falls between −1 and +1 once every cycle.

notes.title: How far into the cycle
notes.explanation: omega t: the angle the cycle has turned through by time t.

notes.title: One half
notes.explanation: Half the peak value of cos squared, which is 1.

notes.title: Angular frequency
notes.explanation: omega: how fast the phase turns, in radians per second.

notes.title: Time
notes.explanation: The time at which the field is read.
